summary: Iteration 5 full-stack testing completed. Cron auth/ack/background digest, tenant regeneration, manufactured due reminder with WhatsApp link, dashboard widget/refresh/empty state, note-tag UI CRUD and customer badge, dashboard contract, quotes CRUD, both logins, auth cookie/bcrypt/lockout, and cron YAML passed. Two backend defects remain: invalid tags on note UPDATE preserve the old tag instead of coercing to empty, and public ingress still returns wildcard CORS for trusted and untrusted origins.

critical.issue: Credentialed CORS preflight returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for both the configured frontend and https://untrusted.example instead of echoing only an explicit trusted origin. FastAPI code is explicit, so the wildcard is likely added/overridden at ingress.

minor.issue: Sending tag='foo' returns 200 but retains the previous valid tag (observed 'borclu') instead of silently coercing the unsupported value to ''. POST correctly coerces it to ''.

ui_bugs.issue: Dashboard emits React missing-key and repeated Recharts ResponsiveContainer width(-1)/height(-1) console warnings during initial render. Charts subsequently render, so this is non-blocking console/runtime noise.

action_items: Change note UPDATE validation to set unsupported tags to '' just like note creation, then retest update persistence and customers.top_tag.
Remove wildcard CORS at ingress/proxy and allow credentialed requests only from explicit configured frontend origins.
Use Europe/Istanbul local date, not UTC date, when keying and fetching daily reminder digests to avoid the 00:00-02:59 Istanbul date boundary mismatch.
Add a unique compound index on reminder_digests(tenant_id, date) to guarantee one digest per tenant/day under concurrent cron/regenerate calls.
Resolve the Dashboard React key and initial Recharts sizing warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: update_customer_note uses the previous tag for unsupported input (`else target.get('tag', '')`), which directly contradicts the documented silent coercion-to-empty contract.

Reminder digest date keys use datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() even though the job is defined in Europe/Istanbul; manual regeneration shortly after Istanbul midnight can read/write the prior UTC day.
reminder_digests has no compound unique index for tenant_id/date, so concurrent upserts can create duplicate daily documents despite the one-document intent.
regenerate_today_digest allows super_admin but then assumes a tenant_id; a super admin has tenant_id=None and can create a meaningless unscoped digest.
server.py is 2,410 lines and combines auth, tenant administration, all business CRUD, reminders/cron, quotes, seeding, and middleware; split it into focused routers/services.

success_rate.backend: 75% (6/8 pytest tests passed; all cron/digest/WhatsApp, dashboard, quote, login, YAML, bcrypt, cookie, and lockout checks passed; note-update coercion and CORS failed)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested UI workflows passed; one low-priority console-warning issue observed

seed_data_creation: Created isolated TEST_I5 API records and a temporary Kazım Öztürk UI customer/note. All customers, notes, motorcycles, quotes, audit traces, and odometer changes were removed/restored. Demo admin password was verified restored to demo123. Today's reminder digest was regenerated after restoration and now has due_count=0.
test_credentials: Used both accounts from /app/memory/test_credentials.md successfully. /app/auth_testing.md is absent. Both hashes start with $2b$; HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=None cookies, five-failure lockout, and seed password-reconciliation code passed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Final iteration-5 pytest is stable at 6 passed/2 failed. Functional cron automation and all requested UI flows pass. Recheck PUT invalid-tag coercion and public trusted/untrusted CORS. Dashboard currently has a zero-link digest after restoration, making empty-state retest straightforward.
rca_of_the_issue: Invalid tag UPDATE is caused by server.py line 869 preserving target.get('tag') when inp.tag is not in _VALID_TAGS; creation instead assigns ''. CORS failure is external to the shown FastAPI allowlist because public preflights return wildcard for both trusted and untrusted origins, indicating ingress/proxy CORS override.
